featured_reviews.name: Jaykrishnan Nambiar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ayyappa Temple Mira Road is a beautiful place to reconnect spiritually, especially if you visit early in the morning. I went around 7 AM, and the calm devotional atmosphere instantly reminded me of temples back in Kerala.

The Pathinettam Padi (sacred 18 steps) carries deep significance for devotees of Lord Ayyappa. While the surroundings here include the usual city hustle,traffic, roads, and urban noise, it still offers a subtle, powerful connection. Of course, it may not replicate the raw, divine aura of Sabarimala Temple nestled amidst dense forests and mountains, but in its own way, it feels like a spiritual “Wi-Fi”- quietly reconnecting you back to your roots in the middle of everyday life.

The morning darshan was peaceful, and receiving prasad added to the wholesome experience. It’s a great place for those who miss that temple energy while managing busy urban routines.

“Tat Tvam Asi” – a profound Sanskrit mahavakya meaning “You are That” or “The divine exists within you.”

Saamiye Sharanam Ayyappa! 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Prabhat Vishwakarma
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Kashi Vishwanath Temple is a famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is located in Vishwanath Gali, near Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India. The temple is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for Shaivites and is among the twelve Jyotirlinga, shrines which are said to be the most sacred abodes of Shiva. Standing on the western banks of the Ganges, the presiding deity is known by the names Shri Vishwanath and Vishweshwara literally meaning Lord of the Universe.
In 1828, Baiza Bai, widow of the Maratha ruler Daulat Rao Scindhia of Gwalior State, built a low-roofed colonnade with over 40 pillars in the Gyan Vapi precinct.During 1833–1840, the boundary of Gyanvapi Well, the ghats and other nearby temples were constructed. Many noble families from various ancestral kingdoms of the Indian subcontinent and their prior establishments make generous contributions for the operations of the temple.
In 1835, Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sikh Empire, on the behest of his wife, Maharani Datar Kaur, donated 1 tonne of gold for plating the temple's dome. In 1841, Raghuji Bhonsle III of Nagpur donated silver to the temple.The temple was managed by a hereditary group of pandits or mahants. After the death of Mahant Devi Dutt, a dispute arose among his successors. In 1900, his brother-in-law Pandit Visheshwar Dayal Tewari, filed a lawsuit, which resulted in him being declared the head priest.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This temple is the perfect destination if you are looking to feel relaxed, calm, and deeply connected to the supreme lord. From the moment you arrive, the vibe is incredibly positive and uplifting, creating a truly serene atmosphere.
One of the highlights is the continuous bhajans (devotional songs) that echo throughout the space, making it easy to leave your worries behind and find a sense of peace.
Beyond the spiritual experience, the temple complex is well-equipped with other amenities. There is a bookshop for those interested in spiritual texts, a food court for casual dining, and the excellent Govinda's restaurant for a more complete meal.
If you want to spend quality time in a calm, peaceful, and spiritually charged environment, this is the best place to be. I highly recommend it.

featured_reviews.name: TANMAY CHOUGULE
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the ISKCON Mira Road Temple and the temple itself is beautiful with a very peaceful and spiritual atmosphere. It is a wonderful place for prayer, meditation, and spending quiet time.

However, I was very disappointed with the behaviour of the security staff. A place like a temple should reflect kindness, patience, and respect. Unfortunately, some security guards were using harsh language with devotees, especially elderly people, and even pushing them while managing the crowd. This kind of behaviour is not appropriate in a spiritual place where people come seeking peace.

I hope the temple management looks into this matter and trains the security staff to treat devotees with more respect and compassion. The temple environment is lovely, but the behaviour of the security staff needs serious improvement.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am deeply grateful to the Maha Vishnu Temple for the care, organization, and support provided during post-death rituals for our family. (12vi or 13vi) The entire process was conducted with dignity, respect, and adherence to traditional customs, which brought a sense of peace and comfort during a difficult time.
The temple staff and priests were compassionate, knowledgeable, and guided us through every step with patience and sensitivity. The arrangements were well-managed, allowing the rituals to be performed smoothly without any unnecessary stress for the family.
The serene atmosphere of the temple further added to the spiritual experience and helped us focus on prayers and remembrance.
A heartfelt thank you to everyone involved. I highly recommend Maha Vishnu Temple to families seeking well-organized and respectful post-death ritual services.

featured_reviews.name: Nithin M Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Google Review # 000365.

Mahavishnu Mandir is a true gem for spiritually inclined residents of Mira Road. This temple, dedicated to the supreme being Lord Vishnu and stands as a serene Deva Sthanam. While primarily dedicated to Lord Vishnu, it houses several other deities. This fosters a sense of unity and harmony among visitors. For Sanatanis, this temple is an absolute must-visit, every month, if not every week. Given the scarcity of Vishnu temples in Mumbai, its presence in Mira Road is particularly significant. It offers a much-needed spiritual retreat for devotees seeking solace and divine blessings.

The interior is spacious, with ample room for meditation. The calming ambiance with regular aartis, creates a spiritually uplifting atmosphere. It is a perfect place to spend some quiet moments in contemplation. Mahavishnu Mandir is a great place to introduce children to culture & spirituality. While the temple offers a wonderful spiritual experience, parking is available on main road.

Overall, Mahavishnu Mandir is a spiritual point that deserves a visit from every resident of Mira Road. It is a place where one can find peace, connect with their inner self, and experience the divine grace of Lord Vishnu and other deities.

Date of Experience # May 2024
